articles.title_original: Momentum quantization of hyperbolic phonon polaritons in photonic-crystal cavity
articles.title_en: h-BN cavity enables quantized hyperbolic phonon polaritons
articles.excerpt_original: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in van der Waals crystals enable extreme electromagnetic confinement and access to exceptionally large in-plane momenta, offering a powerful platform for deep-subwavelength nanophotonics. Although the lower Reststrahlen band (RS1) of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly attractive for low-loss, strongly volume-confined polaritons, fully exploiting this potential remains challenging because RS1 modes are weakly accessible by conventional near-field detection and require efficient leakage suppression for high-Q confinement. Here, we demonstrate that momentum quantization of RS1 HPhPs enables high-Q, ultrasmall mode volume cavity states in an h-BN photonic-crystal nanocavity architecture. Periodic lateral cavity boundaries impose Fabry-Pérot phase matching, while the surrounding photonic-crystal lattice suppresses in-plane leakage and stabilizes discrete cavity-supported momentum states, transforming the continuous hyperbolic dispersion into a ladder of geometry-defined momentum eigenstates. Using photo-induced force microscopy, we directly visualize the quantized cavity modes in real space and reconstruct their discretized dispersion in momentum space. The resulting hyperbolic polaritonic cavity crystal exhibits quality factors exceeding 340 and ultrasmall mode volumes down to V ¯ m = 4.3 × 10 − 7 ( λ 0 / n ) 3 , corresponding to Purcell enhancements approaching 10 7 . This approach establishes a route to high-Q, ultrasmall-volume RS1 polaritonic nanocavities with geometry-defined momentum states, providing a scalable platform for enhanced light-matter interactions, selective vibrational spectroscopy, and reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated high-Q, ultrasmall-volume cavity states in hexagonal boron nitride using a photonic-crystal nanocavity. The approach quantizes polariton momentum and could support enhanced light–matter interactions, vibrational spectroscopy, and mid-infrared nanophotonics.

articles.title_original: Exciton-driven Floquet engineering from first principles
articles.title_en: Exciton-Driven Floquet Engineering Framework Demonstrated in Monolayer hBN
articles.excerpt_original: Floquet engineering uses periodic driving to tailor electronic structures and material properties out of equilibrium. Excitons offer a distinct route to this control: their electron-hole dynamics can act as an internal drive, enabling Floquet engineering beyond direct laser dressing. A microscopic description of this regime requires simultaneous access to excitonic dynamics and their momentum-resolved photoemission signatures, which remains challenging in realistic materials. Here we develop an efficient first-principles framework combining real-time time-dependent density functional theory with a modified long-range-corrected exchange-correlation kernel, Floquet-band analysis, and time- and angle-resolved photoemission simulations. Using monolayer hexagonal boron nitride as a benchmark, we capture a subgap excitonic resonance and show that the resulting oscillatory excitonic field generates clear Floquet sidebands and band renormalization, even without temporal overlap between pump and probe pulses. Our approach establishes a practical and computationally efficient route for predicting nonequilibrium Floquet phenomena driven by collective excitations in quantum materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a first-principles framework combining time-dependent density functional theory, Floquet-band analysis, and photoemission simulations to model exciton-driven nonequilibrium phenomena. Demonstrated in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride, the method predicts Floquet sidebands and band renormalization without temporal overlap between pump and probe pulses.

articles.title_original: Empirical approaches to Fröhlich excitonic polarons in polar semiconductors
articles.title_en: Empirical Models for Excitonic Polarons in Polar Semiconductors

The latter is dominated in ionic crystals by the Fröhlich interaction corresponding to the long-range electric field generated by polar phonons at the zone centre. Theoretical description of complex interplay arising from competition and interference between these two interactions, excitonic and polaronic, has been a formidable challenge. At the same time, the emergence of optoelectronics based on ionic semiconductors such as metal-halide perovskites has made it highly relevant to revisit theoretical models developed in the past, and push them further for application to real ionic semiconductors of interest. To this end, the present paper reviews the physics of Fröhlich excitonic polarons from the point of view of empirical approaches and supplements it with a few original developments to the state-of-the-art. At first, we review the models for excitonic polarons in ionic semiconductors, initially built by Toyozawa and Hermanson in analogy with Lee-Low-Pines (LLP) model for free polarons, and later extended by Pollman and Büttner (PB). These models have been applied in past to the simpler cases of weakly interacting polarons (e.g. GaAs). We further consider their applicability to ionic solids such as TlCl or 3D lead halide perovskites, where the electron-hole correlations are relatively stronger. In these compounds, electrons and holes have almost equal effective masses, which allows us to derive a new analytical expression of the approximated version of the PB effective interaction potential. articles.summary_en: This review examines how excitonic and Fröhlich polaron interactions shape optoelectronic behavior in ionic semiconductors, including lead-halide perovskites. It also develops an analytical approximation for electron–hole interactions in systems with similar effective masses.

articles.title_original: Transient absorption signatures of asymmetric carrier cooling in semiconductors
articles.title_en: Study reveals asymmetric electron and hole cooling in GaN and GaAs
articles.excerpt_original: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used femtosecond transient-absorption spectroscopy and first-principles simulations to distinguish electron and hole cooling in gallium nitride and gallium arsenide. Electron cooling dominates the measured response and occurs on roughly 100-fs timescales, while simulated hole cooling is about an order of magnitude faster.

articles.title_original: Study on synthesis, growth mechanism, and optoelectronic properties of SnZrS3 semiconductor
articles.title_en: Study establishes controlled synthesis route for SnZrS3 semiconductor
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract SnZrS3 is a promising but underexplored chalcogenide semiconductor for optoelectronic applications. Herein, we report a two-step solid-state route in which a highly crystalline ZrS2 intermediate, pre-formed in the first step, reacts with SnS at 600 °C in the second step. Systematic optimization identifies 600 °C, 6 h, and a 1:1 precursor ratio as the optimal conditions. The growth mechanism is elucidated as a template-induced topological transformation in which the morphology of the final SnZrS3 product is inherited from the ZrS2 precursor. DFT calculations reveal an indirect band gap of 1.08 eV, with the valence band edge dominated by S 3p states and the conduction band edge contributed by Zr 4d and Sn 5p states. UV–Vis spectroscopy gives an experimental optical band gap of 1.15 eV, in excellent agreement with the calculated optical band gap 1.14 eV. Raman spectroscopy combined with DFPT calculations identifies the characteristic Ag modes at 158.6 and 330.8 cm-1, assigned to in-plane Sn–S and Zr–S stretching vibrations. These results establish a controllable synthesis route and provide a combined experimental and theoretical understanding of SnZrS3 for photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a two-step solid-state synthesis of crystalline SnZrS3 and identified a template-induced growth mechanism. The material’s approximately 1.15 eV optical band gap supports potential photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications.

articles.excerpt_original: Early cancer screening can significantly improve therapeutic outcomes, volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and other related gases in exhaled breath, as cancer-specific biomarkers, offer a novel approach for non-invasive diagnosis. Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS)-based gas sensors are pivotal for exhaled breath VOCs detection, featuring compact size, cost-effectiveness, and rapid response. This review summarizes the most recent five-year research advances in cancer biomarker detection, and clarifies the core mechanisms of electrical property changes from sensing material-VOCs interactions and key performance metrics including sensitivity, selectivity, humidity tolerance, response/recovery time, stability, and operating temperature. This review also highlights the optimization strategies of sensing materials such as metal doping, surface modification, heterostructure fabrication, and metal oxide-carrier composite synthesis to enhance trace detection, selectivity, and stability via expanded specific surface area, the introduction of active sites and interfacial charge transfer modulation. Finally, this review outlines sensor arrays integrated with machine learning for precise cancer recognition. This review provides theoretical support for the performance optimization and clinical translation of MOS sensors, and facilitates their widespread application in the non-invasive early diagnosis of cancers.

articles.title_en: Laser-induced spin-orbit torques demonstrated in multiferroic GeMnTe
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin‐orbit coupling, and carrier‐mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge 0.85 Mn 0.15 Te using time‐resolved magneto‐optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser‐induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin‐orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser‐induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba‐split, spin‐locked valence band states, and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. The transient change in magnetic properties, observed as variations in the amplitude and coercive field of the pump‐induced change in ellipticity hysteresis loops, is attributed to laser‐induced modifications of the ferroelectric sublattice displacement, which affect the ferroelectric polarization and the associated Rashba spin‐orbit interaction. While the first type of optical spin‐orbit torque has already been observed in the diluted magnetic semiconductor (Ga,Mn)As, the second effect is unique to the multiferroic Rashba semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te, opening new opportunities for all‐optical manipulation of magnetic order and spin‐orbit torque generation in spin‐orbitronic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers observed two laser-induced magnetic effects in the multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te, including coherent magnetization precession and changes in magnetic hysteresis. The findings point to optical control of magnetic order for spin-orbitronic semiconductor devices.

articles.title_original: Inverse design of heterodeformations for strain soliton networks in bilayer 2D materials
articles.title_en: Inverse design enables engineered strain-soliton networks in bilayer graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Strain soliton networks strongly influence the structural and electronic properties of heterodeformed bilayer systems, yet their design remains challenging due to the high-dimensional heterodeformation space and the absence of a direct map between deformation and network geometry. In this work, we introduce a geometric framework that establishes a one-to-one mapping between heterodeformations and the geometry of the strain soliton network expressed as line vector-Burgers vector pairs. The admissible networks are constrained by topology dictated by the generalized stacking fault energy landscape. We show that the moiré Bravais lattice, corresponding to a uniform heterodeformation, alone is insufficient to characterize the interface: distinct heterodeformations can share identical moiré Bravais lattices while producing different soliton networks, reflecting a many-to-one mapping considering translational symmetry only. In contrast, the soliton network encodes the interfacial multilattice geometry, including topology and connectivity, not captured by the moiré Bravais lattice alone. The framework enables the direct construction of heterodeformations from target networks, providing a systematic route for inverse design of moiré interfaces beyond conventional twist-based approaches. Finally, we show that the framework enables the design of symmetry-broken soliton networks in bilayer graphene that exhibit anisotropic (tensorial) interfacial friction, demonstrating its potential for engineering superlubric interfaces.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a geometric framework linking heterodeformations to the topology and connectivity of strain-soliton networks in bilayer 2D materials. The approach enables design of symmetry-broken bilayer graphene interfaces with anisotropic friction, supporting future engineering of moiré and superlubric interfaces.

articles.title_original: Electrically tunable two-dimensional quantum materials for terahertz optoelectronics
articles.title_en: Electrically Tunable 2D Materials Advance Terahertz Optoelectronics
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional (2D) quantum materials host electronic and collective excitations whose characteristic energies naturally fall within the terahertz (THz) range. Their reduced dimensionality, strong light–matter interaction, and sensitivity to external fields provide opportunities for electrically reconfigurable THz optoelectronics that are difficult to realize using conventional semiconductors and passive optical materials. In this review, we examine how electrical control of carrier density, dielectric screening, ferroelectric polarization, and correlated electronic states can program the THz response of diverse 2D quantum materials, including topological semimetals, semiconductors with strong excitonic effects, ferroelectrics, as well as their moiré superlattices. We first outline the fundamental THz optoelectronic processes, including generation, detection, and modulation, together with the main limitations of conventional materials and device platforms. We then discuss the distinctive properties of major 2D quantum-material platforms that govern their THz response. Recent progress is subsequently reviewed according to the main electrical tuning mechanisms, including electrostatic doping, displacement-field control, and ferroelectric polarization switching. We introduce how these approaches modify THz properties of 2D quantum materials and how the resulting tunability is used in THz optoelectronics with competitive performance and superior electrical tunability. We conclude by discussing the key challenges and promising future research directions that could advance high-performance, intelligent, and multifunctional THz optoelectronics based on electrically tunable 2D quantum materials.
articles.summary_en: A review examines how carrier-density control, dielectric screening, ferroelectric switching, and correlated states enable electrically reconfigurable terahertz generation, detection, and modulation. The work highlights tunable two-dimensional platforms and identifies challenges for high-performance multifunctional THz devices.

articles.title_original: Energy‐Transfer Pathways for Photoluminescence in Mn 2+ ‐Doped 2D Hybrid Lead Bromide Systems
articles.title_en: Study maps energy-transfer pathways in Mn²⁺-doped 2D lead bromide systems
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Mn 2+ doping in hybrid perovskite‐derived two‐dimensional (2D) lead bromide systems exhibits efficient Mn 2+ emission and enhanced environmental stability compared to their 3D analogue perovskites. Here, we investigate the sensitization of Mn 2+ emission in doped 2D BA 2 PbBr 4 (BA = butylammonium) through comprehensive temperature‐dependent PL analyses. We establish a near‐resonant energy transfer from the host excitonic state to the higher‐lying Mn 2+ multiplet ( 4 T 2g (D)), followed by successive multiphonon‐assisted de‐excitations through the intermediate multiplets of Mn 2+ between the originally populated 4 T 2g (D) and the first excited multiplet, 4 T 1g (G) state. Infrared (IR) spectroscopy identifies the highest‐energy phonon mode at 59.2 meV in BA 2 PbBr 4 , more than twice that of the previously analyzed 3D perovskite CsPbCl 3 nanocrystals, pointing to a significantly more efficient multiphonon relaxation and suppressed phonon bottleneck effects in the 2D case, explaining the efficient Mn 2+ emission observed even at low temperatures. The contrasting behaviors are further accentuated by the significantly higher exciton binding energy in the 2D case compared to the 3D ones. We derive temperature‐dependent rate equations to quantitatively explain host‐to‐dopant energy‐transfer dynamics, identifying the role of dark excitonic states in near‐resonant energy‐transfer and back‐transfer processes, establishing a comprehensive understanding of Mn 2+ emission in such 2D hybrid lead bromide systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers identify near-resonant host-to-Mn²⁺ energy transfer followed by multiphonon relaxation in 2D BA₂PbBr₄. Higher-energy phonons and stronger exciton binding help explain efficient low-temperature photoluminescence and reduced phonon bottleneck effects.

articles.title_original: Oxygen-Assisted Direct Synthesis of Two-Dimensional Ferroelectric Bi2SeO5
articles.title_en: Oxygen-Assisted Direct Synthesis of 2D Ferroelectric Bi₂SeO₅
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectrics are promising for nonvolatile memory, nanoelectronics, and neuromorphic devices. Among them, bismuth selenite (Bi2SeO5) has recently emerged as a high-performance van der Waals (vdW) ferroelectric oxide. However, its current synthesis mainly relies on the post-oxidation of Bi2O2Se, which complicates the fabrication process and limits its integration potential. Here, we report the oxygen-assisted direct synthesis of 2D ferroelectric Bi2SeO5 nanosheets by regulating the oxygen chemical potential and the resulting relative thermodynamic stability of competing Bi–Se–O phases. The presence of O2 increases the oxygen chemical potential, rendering Bi2SeO5 thermodynamically more stable than Bi2O2Se and enabling its direct growth. The as-grown Bi2SeO5 nanosheets exhibit high crystallinity, uniform composition, well-defined chemical states, and robust in-plane (IP) and out-of-plane (OOP) ferroelectricity, while temperature-dependent second-harmonic generation (SHG) measurements reveal that the non-centrosymmetric phase persists up to approximately 690 K. Lateral and vertical devices further demonstrate stable polarization-controlled resistive switching. This work establishes a direct synthesis route to 2D ferroelectric Bi2SeO5 and provides a foundation for ferroelectric memory and nanoelectronic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a direct oxygen-assisted growth method for highly crystalline Bi₂SeO₅ nanosheets, avoiding post-oxidation of Bi₂O₂Se. The material shows ferroelectricity up to approximately 690 K and stable polarization-controlled resistive switching, supporting potential use in nonvolatile memory and nanoelectronics.

articles.title_original: Coherent Electronic Lensing in Proximitized Graphene
articles.title_en: Scanning-Gate Microscopy Controls Electron Lensing in Graphene Josephson Junctions
articles.excerpt_original: Spatially resolved control of coherent electron transport offers a route to understanding and engineering interference phenomena in hybrid superconducting devices. Here, we use Scanning Gate Microscopy (SGM) to investigate Fabry-Pérot (FP) interference in the n-p-n cavity of a ballistic graphene Josephson junction. Spatial maps of the superconducting switching current and normal-state conductance reveal circular interference fringes arising from two distinct effects of the SGM tip potential. A global shift of the Fermi wave vector modulates the FP resonances of the cavity, while a local perturbation produces additional oscillations that persist at fixed Fermi wave vector as the tip bias is varied. An analytical model identifies the origin of this local response with coherent electron lensing, in which the tip modifies the phase accumulated along interfering trajectories. The measured fringe patterns in the switching current indicate that this mechanism affects superconducting transport, consistent with tip-induced shifts of the resonance conditions for Andreev bound states. These results establish SGM as a tunable local lens for controlling interference in superconducting ballistic graphene devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated coherent electron lensing in a ballistic graphene Josephson junction using scanning-gate microscopy. The findings show that local electrostatic perturbations can tune interference and superconducting transport through Andreev bound states, supporting new control strategies for graphene-based quantum devices.

articles.title_original: General formulas for calculating the ballistic conductance of two-dimensional Dirac materials
articles.title_en: Study derives ballistic conductance formulas for 2D Dirac materials
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract One important electrical quantity in devices is the conductance; for systems on the mesoscopic scale and nanoscale, the conductance is given by the Landauer–Büttiker formalism. In this paper, by using the minimal Weyl Hamiltonian, a theoretical study on the ballistic conductance of two-dimensional Dirac materials is carried out, with the aim of deriving properties of the ballistic conductance. In addition, formulas for calculating and comparing the ballistic conductance of Dirac materials with diverse cones are given. Our study reveals that the ballistic conductance can be both isotropic and anisotropic, depending on the values of the Dirac cone characteristics (i.e. the anisotropy and tilt). The effects of the anisotropy and tilt of the Dirac cone on the ballistic conductance are investigated in detail. For the right Dirac cone, we show that the ballistic conductance in the x direction does not depend on the strength of the anisotropy of Dirac cone, while the ballistic conductance in the y direction varies inversely with the strength of anisotropy. We find that the ballistic conductance of the oblique Dirac cone is greater than that of the right Dirac cone. Also, when the strength of tilt increases, that is, when the Dirac cone becomes more tilted, the ballistic conductance rises. We also investigate symmetry properties of the ballistic conductance. This paper provides a new and deeper insight into properties of the ballistic conductance from massless Dirac fermions and can be useful for designing electronic devices with desired performance.
articles.summary_en: IOP Publishing research develops theoretical formulas for calculating ballistic conductance in two-dimensional Dirac materials with varying cone anisotropy and tilt. The results could inform the design of electronic devices with tailored conductance, but no specific material, company, or device demonstration is reported.

articles.title_original: A Graphene-Based Tunable Metamaterial Absorber with Transmission in the Terahertz Band for Refractive Index Sensing
articles.title_en: Graphene-Based Tunable Terahertz Metamaterial Enables Refractive-Index Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: A tunable terahertz metamaterial absorber with transmission characteristics is proposed and numerically studied. The proposed four-layer structure of the absorber comprises a patterned gold resonator, a patterned graphene layer, a silicon dioxide (SiO2) substrate, and a bottom gold layer. Unlike other common designs reported in the literature that block the transmission of electromagnetic waves using a bottom metal plane, the proposed design allows for the transmission of electromagnetic waves by using a slotted gold-metallic ground plane. Through simulation analysis, it is found that a high absorption of 97.3% occurs at 0.9512 THz, while a transmission peak of 90% occurs at 0.440 THz, thus proving high absorption and non-zero transmission in a small structure. The impedance is 420 Ω at 0.9512 THz, which is close to the characteristic impedance of air (377 Ω), indicating the effective coupling of the electromagnetic waves to the absorber with minimized reflection at the air interface. The ability to tune the resonance response dynamically with graphene is achieved by tuning the chemical potential and relaxation time. The absorber also shows polarization-insensitive performance and large-angle stability as large as 70° for both TE and TM modes. Apart from this, it is shown that the proposed metamaterial absorber also has the ability of refractive-index sensing with a sensitivity of 0.1488 THz/RIU.
articles.summary_en: Researchers numerically modeled a four-layer graphene–gold metamaterial absorber with 97.3% absorption at 0.9512 THz and 90% transmission at 0.440 THz. Graphene tuning enables dynamic resonance control, polarization-insensitive operation, and refractive-index sensing with a reported sensitivity of 0.1488 THz/RIU.

articles.title_original: On the Mechanism of the Oxygen Reduction Reaction on Nitrogen-Doped Graphenes in Alkaline Media
articles.title_en: Nitrogen-Doped Graphene Favors Outer-Sphere Oxygen Reduction in Alkaline Media
articles.excerpt_original: Nitrogen-doped graphene-like materials exhibit high catalytic activity and stability in the oxygen reduction reaction. Theoretical studies of catalytic activity based on DFT calculations typically assume that the reaction proceeds via an inner-sphere mechanism involving the chemisorption of an oxygen molecule. In this work, using grand-canonical DFT calculations we demonstrate that, in an alkaline medium, an outer-sphere reaction mechanism, initiated with an electron transfer to a solvated O2 molecule near the surface, is energetically more favorable. On N-doped graphene containing graphitic nitrogen atoms, the reaction proceeds via a 4e mechanism due to a significant reduction in the chemisorption energy of the *OH intermediate, whereas on pristine graphene, the reaction terminates after two electron transfers.
articles.summary_en: Grand-canonical DFT calculations indicate that oxygen reduction on nitrogen-doped graphene proceeds more favorably through an outer-sphere mechanism initiated by electron transfer to solvated oxygen. Graphitic nitrogen enables a four-electron pathway by weakening hydroxyl intermediate chemisorption, while pristine graphene stops after two electron transfers.

articles.title_original: Systematic screening study toward zero bilateral carrier injection barrier in WSe2-MXene heterojunctions
articles.title_en: Screening WSe₂–MXene Heterojunctions for Barrier-Free Carrier Injection
articles.summary_en: A systematic study screens WSe₂–MXene heterojunctions for configurations with zero bilateral carrier-injection barriers. The work could inform materials selection for semiconductor heterostructures and electronic devices.

articles.title_original: Biomimetic hydrophobic gating in MXene polypyrrole–based artificial Ion channels for efficient perchlorate sensing
articles.title_en: MXene–Polypyrrole Sensor Enables Highly Selective Perchlorate Detection
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Ion selective electrodes represent a promising approach for ion detection based on potentiometric sensing principle. However, their practical application is often hampered by insufficient selectivity, primarily caused by interference from structurally similar ions. Herein, inspired by biological potassium ion channels, we demonstrate an efficient perchlorate ion selective electrode via the self–assembly of pyrrole–functionalized MXene nanosheets and methylated quaternary ammonium compounds. The resulting composite sensor significantly outperforms commercial ion selective electrodes with a > 10 4 –fold lower detection limit (10 –9.7 M), 18–fold higher selectivity ( K ij of 130.4), and a maximum sensitivity up to 59.6 mV/dec for perchlorate. Synchrotron X–ray scattering and mechanistic studies attribute this superior performance to a hydrophobic gating mechanism arising from dehydration effects and transport resistance within confined channels, which effectively lowers the energy barrier for perchlorate transport by 12.13 kcal/mol compared to that of sulfate. Furthermore, the sensor was optimized via substituent engineering for broad-spectrum anion detection and integrated into a portable platform for continuous on–site monitoring, achieving accuracy comparable to ion chromatography in real–world scenarios.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a biomimetic MXene–polypyrrole ion-selective sensor for perchlorate, reporting a detection limit of 10⁻⁹·⁷ M and substantially improved selectivity over commercial electrodes. A portable version supported continuous on-site monitoring with accuracy comparable to ion chromatography.

articles.title_original: MXene@C/SiO 2 composite films with layered heterostructures for high-temperature infrared stealth, electromagnetic interference shielding, and fire safety
articles.title_en: MXene–C/SiO₂ Films Combine Infrared Stealth, EMI Shielding and Fire Resistance
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Flexible materials integrating infrared stealth, electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, thermal management, and fire safety are highly desirable for aerospace and high-temperature electronics. Here, layered MXene@C/SiO2 composite films (MCSx) with tunable structural units were constructed by combining low-thermal-conductivity C/SiO2 nanofiber layers with highly conductive MXene layers. This heterogeneous architecture endows the films with pronounced anisotropic thermal transport and an ultralow through-plane thermal conductivity of 0.030 W m−1 K−1. Benefiting from the low emissivity of MXene and efficient thermal insulation, the films achieve infrared stealth over 50–500 °C and reduce the apparent surface temperature by 365.7 °C at a heat source temperature of 500 °C. The continuous MXene network enables rapid Joule heating from 29.5 to 149.6 °C at 0.5–3.0 V with an electrothermal conversion efficiency exceeding 99%. The conductive layers and heterogeneous interfaces jointly achieve an X-band EMI shielding effectiveness of 71.6 dB. The films also exhibit excellent flame retardancy, thermal insulation, and fire resistance while maintaining EMI shielding performance after flame exposure. This work provides a heterostructure engineering strategy for developing multifunctional protective materials under thermally demanding conditions.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed layered MXene@C/SiO₂ composite films with ultralow through-plane thermal conductivity, infrared stealth from 50–500 °C, and 71.6 dB X-band electromagnetic-interference shielding. The flexible films also support efficient Joule heating and retain shielding performance after flame exposure, indicating potential for aerospace and high-temperature electronics protection.

articles.title_original: A Ti3C2Tx MXén jellemzése, fotokatalitikus alkalmazása és környezeti hatásai: Characterization, photocatalytic applications and environmental effects of Ti3C2Tx MXene
articles.title_en: Ti3C2Tx MXene Shows Photocatalytic Effects and Concentration-Dependent Toxicity
articles.excerpt_original: In the present work, the characterization and photocatalytic activity of two different catalysts (P25 TiO2, ZnO) was investigated in the presence of Ti3C2Tx MXene to assess its effect on their photocatalytic performance. The samples were further characterized using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS), X-Ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The potential effects of Ti3C2Tx MXene on living organisms (isopods) were also evaluated over a 4-week period at different concentrations (0.1%, 0.5% and 1.5% relative to soil), alongside a control group. The effects of MXene exposure on isopod morphology, including body mass, and mortality were assessed, including the determination of the LD₅₀ value. Based on the results obtained to date, P25 TiO2 showed no detectable toxic effects, whereas increasing the MXene concentration resulted in a slightly increase in the toxicity of the composites. A minták vizsgálata pásztázó elekron mikroszkópiával (SEM), diffúz reflektancia spektroszkópiával (DRS) és röntgen fotoelektron spektroszkópiával (XPS) valósult meg. A Ti3C2Tx MXén élő szervezetekre (kis pinceászka) gyakorolt lehetséges hatásait szintén értékeltük egy 4 hetes kísérlet során, különböző koncentrációkban (0,1%, 0,5% és 1,5% a talajhoz viszonyítva), kontrollcsoport mellett. Az ászkarákok testtömegének változását és mortalitásukra gyakorolt hatását mértük, beleértve az LD₅₀-érték meghatározását is. Az eddig kapott eredmények alapján a P25 TiO2 nem mutatott kimutatható toxikus hatást, míg az MXén koncentrációjának növelése a k
articles.summary_en: Researchers characterized Ti3C2Tx MXene combined with P25 TiO2 and ZnO catalysts and assessed its photocatalytic performance using SEM, DRS and XPS. A four-week isopod study found no detectable toxicity from P25 TiO2, while increasing MXene concentrations slightly increased composite toxicity.

articles.title_original: Drift-induced nonreciprocity in image-polariton-mediated dipole emission
articles.title_en: Drift-Biased Graphene Enables Directional Nanoscale Light Coupling
articles.excerpt_original: Electrical current bias offers a magnet-free route to nonreciprocal light propagation at the nanoscale. Here, we theoretically explore drift-induced nonreciprocity in graphene heterostructures containing hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), where graphene plasmons interact with hBN phonon polaritons in the infrared. Both the random-phase approximation and the Boltzmann transport equation are used to characterize the nonlocal optical response of drift-biased graphene. We compare graphene on hBN with an image-polaritonic structure comprising graphene, a thin hBN spacer, and a gold substrate. Carrier drift produces pronounced directional shifts of the polariton dispersion, while coupling to hBN phonon polaritons strongly modifies the nonreciprocal response. In the image-polaritonic structure, the graphene polaritons become up to twice as confined while retaining a comparable Fizeau shift. The nonreciprocal polariton dispersion produces directional near-field emission and nonreciprocal dipole-dipole interactions, the latter quantified through the cross density of optical states, reaching a left-right dissymmetry of up to ~40%. Our results identify image polaritons in drift-biased graphene as a compact, electrically tunable platform for directional coupling between quantum emitters at the nanoscale.
articles.summary_en: Theoretical modeling shows that electrical carrier drift in graphene–hBN heterostructures can produce nonreciprocal polariton dispersion and directional near-field emission without a magnetic field. An image-polaritonic graphene/hBN/gold structure reportedly doubles polariton confinement and achieves up to ~40% left-right dissymmetry in dipole interactions, indicating potential for electrically tunable nanoscale photonic coupling.

articles.title_original: Collective sliding relaxor ferroelectricity across thousand-layer van der Waals superstructures
articles.title_en: Stacked Boron Nitride Shows Giant Sliding Relaxor Ferroelectricity
articles.excerpt_original: Relaxor ferroelectrics are among the most important electromechanical materials owing to their exceptionally large electrostrictive responses. However, conventional relaxor behavior is generally associated with chemical complexity and structural disorder, where local compositional fluctuations generate polar nanoregions, making the microscopic origin of this behavior difficult to control and engineer. Here we report sliding relaxor ferroelectricity (S-RFE), a previously unknown relaxor state in which engineered stacking-phase heterogeneity enables cooperative interlayer sliding to generate collective relaxor behavior. Through stacking-phase engineering in rhombohedral boron nitride, we create sliding domains that act as structural analogues of polar nanoregions and cooperatively align under an electric field through interlayer sliding. This collective state produces reversible electromechanical deformation of up to approximately $-1.6\%$ with negligible hysteresis in approximately 300-nm-thick crystals, corresponding to approximately 1000 atomic layers. The resulting electrostriction coefficient ($Q_{33}$ of approximately $1200\,\mathrm{m}^{4}\mathrm{C}^{-2}$) exceeds those of most crystalline electrostrictors by orders of magnitude. Unlike conventional relaxors, whose electromechanical response is often suppressed by dipolar freezing at low temperatures, S-RFE remains active down to 1.6 K and maintains giant electromechanical functionality. Our results establish sliding relaxor ferroelectricity as a new route to relaxor behavior and reveal how atomic-scale interlayer motion can be amplified into collective mesoscale functionality across approximately one thousand layers, providing a materials-by-design platform for electromechanical, photonic, and quantum technologies
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a previously unknown relaxor state in rhombohedral boron nitride, created through engineered stacking-phase heterogeneity and cooperative interlayer sliding. The approximately 1.6% reversible deformation and exceptional electrostriction remain active down to 1.6 K, suggesting potential for electromechanical, photonic, and quantum technologies.

articles.title_original: Graphene-Nanoplatelet-Induced π–π Ordering in Electrodeposited Graphene/PANI Nanocomposite Thin Films: Bandgap Narrowing, Dielectric-Loss Modulation, and Enhanced Charge Transport
articles.title_en: Graphene Nanoplatelets Improve Conductivity and Narrow Bandgap in PANI Thin Films
articles.excerpt_original: Camphorsulfonic-acid-doped polyaniline/graphene nanoplatelet (PANI/GNPs) thin films were electrodeposited on indium tin oxide to determine how GNP loading affects film structure and optical, dielectric, and electrical properties. Pristine PANI and composite films were prepared at a constant cell bias using GNP feed loadings of 6, 12, and 18 wt.% relative to aniline. White-light interferometry and scanning electron microscopy revealed a non-monotonic morphological evolution: low GNP loading increased surface roughness, whereas higher loadings produced more consolidated but heterogeneous structures, consistent with changes in PANI growth around the graphene nanoplatelets. FTIR spectra retained the characteristic PANI backbone and emeraldine-salt-related bands; changes in band width and intensity were consistent with altered chain packing and non-covalent interactions at PANI/GNP interfaces. UV–Vis–NIR measurements showed reduced transmittance, enhanced optical attenuation, and changes in refractive-index dispersion. The optical bandgap estimated using the direct-transition Tauc model decreased from 2.49 eV for pristine PANI to 2.17 eV at 18 wt.% GNP feed loading. The calculated surface and volume energy-loss functions increased with GNP loading, indicating changes in the optical dielectric response. Reported room-temperature DC conductivity increased from 0.9 to 1.5 S cm−1, consistent with improved charge transport through the PANI/GNP network. Analysis of X-ray diffraction in q-space identified additional ordered scattering features in the composite films, including characteristic spacings of approximately 3.22–3.26 Å tentatively associated with stacking of the graphene layers within GNPs. These results link GNP feed loading to changes in film morphology, optical respons
articles.summary_en: Researchers electrodeposited polyaniline/graphene nanoplatelet composite films and found that increasing graphene loading reduced the optical bandgap from 2.49 to 2.17 eV. Room-temperature conductivity also increased from 0.9 to 1.5 S cm−1, alongside changes in morphology, dielectric response, and graphene-layer ordering.

articles.title_original: Manipulating anomalous transport via crystal symmetry in two-dimensional altermagnets
articles.title_en: Crystal symmetry controls anomalous transport in 2D altermagnets
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate how crystal symmetry can manipulate anomalous transport phenomena in two-dimensional altermagnetic materials. The findings may inform future spintronic and magnetic-device designs, although no commercial application is identified.

articles.title_original: Integrated vanadium oxide cathodes with MXene for enhanced Zn2+ storage and structural stability
articles.title_en: MXene-Integrated Vanadium Oxide Cathodes Improve Zinc-Ion Storage
articles.summary_en: Academic research reports vanadium oxide cathodes integrated with MXene to enhance Zn2+ storage performance and structural stability. The work indicates a potentially more durable cathode architecture for zinc-ion batteries, although no commercial or company involvement is identified.

articles.title_original: Molecular Dynamic Simulation Of Graphene With Void
articles.title_en: Molecular dynamics study finds voided graphene stable across aerospace temperatures
articles.excerpt_original: Graphene is widely used in the manufacture of composite materials for aerospace applications. This study investigates the effect of temperature changes on its mechanical properties of void-graphene nanosheets (VGNs). In order to achieve this goal, PGNs samples were prepared using a recently developed computational tool called “LUNAR”, which stands for “LAMMPS Utility for Network Analysis and Reactivity”. The “LAMMPS” tool was also used, “LAMMPS” stands for “Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator”, which is used to perform “Molecular Dynamics (MD) modeling “and simulate the PGNs mechanical behavior utilizing the “Polymer Consistent Force Field (PCFF)”.Other computational tools were used, such as “OVITO and QtiPlot” were utilized to collect and analyze the obtained data using precise scientific techniques.The simulation was performed within a temperature range between 200 ºK to 350 ºK (-73.15 ºC to 76.85 ºC). This temperature range is commonly applied for aerospace structures. This research concludes that VGNs are only slightly affected within the proposed temperature ranges, which explains the use of graphene in space applications. Molecular dynamics simulations provide clear evidence of the mechanical and thermal stability of graphene. Graphene exhibits a slight and consistent decrease in mechanical properties with increasing temperature. Additionally, this study has demonstrated that the PCFF force field used to simulate VGNs is computationally inexpensive (fast), and possesses efficiency, accuracy, and produce reliable results. Thus, the methodology used in this study can be used as a reliable computational modeling procedure to speed up the development of aerospace structures.
articles.summary_en: A molecular dynamics study simulated voided graphene nanosheets from 200–350 K, finding only a slight decline in mechanical properties as temperature increased. The results support graphene’s potential use in aerospace structures and validate a computational workflow for faster materials development.

articles.title_original: A comprehensive review on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs)/MXene composites for photocatalytic applications: design principles, mechanisms, and performance trends
articles.title_en: Review examines MOF/MXene composites for photocatalysis
articles.summary_en: A comprehensive review analyzes design principles, mechanisms, and performance trends in metal-organic framework/MXene composites for photocatalytic applications. The study is relevant to materials research but does not identify a specific commercial development or company.

articles.title_original: Graphene Steel Slag in Cement Composites: Piezoresistivity and Damage Monitoring
articles.title_en: Graphene–Steel Slag Cement Composites Enable Piezoresistive Damage Monitoring
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract This study proposes a damage model for cement-based composites incorporating graphene and steel slag.Conducted piezoresistive experiments to analyze the effects of varying steel slag content and the synergistic interaction between graphene and steel slag on the piezoresistive properties. Selected the optimal mixture ratio for further investigation based on the results.An integrated damage monitoring methodology combining ultrasonic emission systems, electrical signal acquisition systems, and digital image correlation (DIC) was employed to track the internal damage evolution in cement-based composites in real time. This approach enables synergistic analysis of multi-source data, providing comprehensive characterization of both damage behavior and strain distribution.The results demonstrate that the proposed damage model effectively predicts internal damage evolution in cement-based composites under both monotonic and cyclic loading conditions, providing a reliable new methodology for early-stage failure warning in concrete structures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed graphene and steel-slag cement composites with piezoresistive properties for tracking internal damage. Combining electrical signals, ultrasonic emissions and digital image correlation enabled real-time monitoring and early failure-warning assessment under monotonic and cyclic loading.

articles.title_original: Next-generation ultra-broadband and angularly stable MXene-based solar absorber with multilayer resonance engineering and AI-driven performance optimization
articles.title_en: AI-Optimized MXene Solar Absorber Achieves Ultra-Broadband, Angular-Stable Absorption
articles.excerpt_original: For sustained energy collection over a wide range of the spectrum, efficient solar thermal absorbers are crucial. In this research work, a multilayer MXene-based solar absorber is designed and systematically investigated to achieve ultra-broadband and high-efficiency absorption. The proposed structure consists of MXene and SiO 2 , with MXene used in a patterned resonator layer, a dielectric SiO 2 spacer, and a continuous MXene ground layer that suppresses transmission. Finite Element Method (FEM) numerical simulation results demonstrate near-unity absorption across the 200–2500 nm wavelength range, with a peak absorptance approaching 100% and an average absorption of approximately 96%. Parametric optimization analysis reveals that variations in structural length, resonator thickness, spacer thickness, and ground layer thickness have minimal impact on overall absorption, confirming strong design robustness and fabrication tolerance. Angular analysis shows stable absorption performance up to large incident angles, ensuring effective solar harvesting throughout the day without tracking systems. Electric field distributions at representative wavelengths illustrate multiple absorption mechanisms, including edge localization, interlayer coupling, and cavity resonance within the MXene layer. Furthermore, a machine learning (ML)–assisted optimization framework is employed to accurately predict absorption behaviour, achieving high R 2 values and low prediction errors, thereby significantly reducing computational effort. The combined numerical and data-driven results confirm that the proposed MXene absorber is a promising candidate for high-performance solar thermal and renewable energy applications.

articles.excerpt_original: Abstract We develop a first-principles approach based on maximally localized Wannier functions for the calculation of higher order multipolar response properties in crystals including dipole–quadrupole, quadrupole–quadrupole, and dipole-octupole polarizabilities. The method is based on an interpolation procedure of the electronic structure of materials, and it is formulated by extending molecular perturbation theory to periodic crystals. General symmetry considerations are used to determine relations between different components and to prove that the dipole–quadrupole polarizability vanishes in centrosymmetric systems. The approach is applied to compute and analyze the multipole–multipole polarizabilities of several representative materials, including centrosymmetric systems (bulk graphite, h-BN, MoS2, and 2H-phase WTe2) and noncentrosymmetric ones (bulk Td–WTe2 and bulk Te). The multipole–multipole polarizabilities are further related to optical gyration with specific application to Te and Td–WTe2. The proposed algorithm possesses several advantages, including conceptual simplicity, computational efficiency, and relatively low computational cost for the computation of multipolar response in materials.
articles.summary_en: Researchers present an ab initio method using maximally localized Wannier functions to calculate higher-order multipolar polarizabilities in periodic materials. articles.title_original: The Boron–Neuron Connection: The Potential of Boron‐Containing Molecules for Treating Incurable Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
articles.title_en: Boron-Containing Molecules Show Potential for ALS Treatment
articles.excerpt_original: BACKGROUND: ) geometries enable dynamic covalent interactions with biological nucleophiles, making boron-containing compounds (BCCs) attractive pharmacophores that selectively interact with reactive oxygen species (ROS) and are ROS-responsive for therapeutic development. BCCs possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and metal-chelating properties that make them attractive candidates for neurodegenerative diseases. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a fatal and multifactorial motor neurodegenerative disorder, is characterized by oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and metal dyshomeostasis, providing a strong rationale for exploring boron-based therapeutics. METHODS: This review examines current literature on B chemistry, pharmacology, and translational applications, with emphasis on mechanisms relevant to ALS pathogenesis. This review focuses on ROS-responsive B scaffolds, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, neuroprotective mechanisms, hormonal modulation, metal chelation, and emerging preclinical evidence supporting boron-based interventions. CONCLUSIONS: BCCs represent a promising yet underexplored therapeutic platform for ALS and related neurodegenerative disorders. Their ROS-responsive, redox-modulating, and neuroprotective properties, combined with favorable CNS drug-like pharmacokinetics, offer a mechanistically distinct approach to disease modification. Emerging preclinical evidence strongly supports further translational investigation.
articles.summary_en: A review examines boron-containing compounds as potential therapeutics for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, focusing on ROS responsiveness, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity, metal chelation, and blood–brain barrier permeability. articles.title_original: Group Representations in Two- and Three-Dimensional Kakeya Geometry
articles.title_en: Representation Theory Framework for Kakeya Geometry
articles.excerpt_original: Kakeya geometry asks how small a subset of Euclidean space can be while containing a unit line segment in every direction. The problem is central to harmonic analysis because its tube formulations are closely related to maximal operators, Fourier restriction, and oscillatory integrals. This paper provides an analysis of the two-dimensional and three-dimensional Kakeya problems from the perspectives of group action and representation theory. This paper first passes from Kakeya sets to finite families of thin tubes, where dimension is studied through tube number, multiplicity, and union volume. It then describes an oriented line by its direction and transverse position and identify the line space as the homogeneous space L n + ≅ S E ( n ) / ( R × S O ( n − 1 ) ) . The Euclidean action on points and lines induces quasi-regular representations, and the X-ray transform becomes an intertwining operator satisfying X π ( g ) = π ^ ( g ) X . In two dimensions, this framework organizes translation invariance, Fourier analysis, and angular almost orthogonality. In three dimensions, spherical harmonics and affine rescaling organize directional and scale information, while additional positional and multiscale correlations explain why symmetry alone is insufficient. The resulting formulation does not provide a new Kakeya estimate; instead, it gives a unified language for comparing the planar and spatial problems and for isolating the geometric difficulties that remain in higher dimensions.
articles.summary_en: Researchers develop a unified representation-theoretic framework for two- and three-dimensional Kakeya problems, linking tube geometry with group actions, Fourier analysis, and X-ray transforms. The work clarifies persistent geometric challenges but does not provide a new Kakeya estimate.

articles.title_original: Pyro‐Phototronic Effect in Two‐Dimensional Graphene/AgCrP 2 S 6 /Graphene Heterojunction
articles.title_en: Graphene/AgCrP₂S₆ heterojunction boosts photodetector performance via pyro-phototronics
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT The pyro‐phototronic effect has been identified as a promising strategy for improving the performance of photodetectors. In this study, we report the discovery of the pyro‐phototronic effect in the graphene/AgCrP 2 S 6 /graphene (Gr/AgCrP 2 S 6 /Gr) heterojunction. Multilayer AgCrP 2 S 6 exhibits a non‐centrosymmetric structure induced by interlayer sliding, as experimentally verified by second‐harmonic generation (SHG) and piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM). Furthermore, the fabricated Gr/AgCrP 2 S 6 /Gr heterojunction, which exhibits a peak pyroelectric coefficient of 9638 µC·m −2 ·K −1 . The pyro‐phototronic effect of the heterojunction is systematically investigated under varying wavelengths, optical power intensities, bias voltages, and modulation frequencies. The pyro‐phototronic effect markedly enhances the heterojunction's output current density, achieving a remarkable 14.57‐fold increase relative to the performance based solely on the photovoltaic effect. Specifically, under 405 nm illumination, the heterojunction achieves peak photodetection metrics: responsivity of 46.01 mA/W, external quantum efficiency of 14.09%, and specific detectivity of 2.2 × 10 11 Jones. These findings deepen the understanding of multi‐field coupling mechanisms in 2D materials and establish a new paradigm for the design and development of high‐performance photodetectors leveraging the pyro‐phototronic effect.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated a pyro-phototronic effect in a graphene/AgCrP₂S₆/graphene heterojunction, increasing output current density 14.57-fold over photovoltaic operation alone. Under 405 nm illumination, the device reached 46.01 mA/W responsivity and 2.2 × 10¹¹ Jones detectivity, indicating potential for advanced 2D-material photodetectors.

articles.title_original: Plasmons of graphene and monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides double-layer
articles.title_en: Graphene–TMD Double Layers Show Tunable Plasmon Modes
articles.excerpt_original: We investigate the plasmonic properties of a double-layer structure consisting of graphene and monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (ML-TMDs) separated by a space distance $d$ where the carrier densities in different layers are $n_1$ and $n_2$ within the usual standard random-phase approximation (RPA) dielectric function approach. There exists two branches of plasmons for an acoustical mode and an optical mode, respectively. We examine the effect of carrier density, inter-layer spacing, and types of TMDs materials on the plasmon properties. Meanwhile, the two branches of plasmons have nonzero decay rates after entering the Landau damping regions for intra-band and inter-band single-particle excitation (SPE) continuum. The plasmons in double-layer structure exhibit significant tunability, offering promising applications of 2D materials for plasmonic devices.
articles.summary_en: Researchers model plasmonic behavior in double layers combining graphene with monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides. The two acoustic and optical plasmon branches can be tuned through carrier density, layer spacing, and TMD composition, indicating potential for plasmonic devices.

articles.title_original: Quantum energy storage in graphene SNS junctions
articles.title_en: Study explores quantum energy storage in graphene Josephson junctions
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract We investigate quantum energy storage in graphene superconductor-normal-superconductor (SNS) Josephson junctions from the perspective of Andreev bound-state(ABS) dynamics. Within the Dirac-Bogoliubov-de Gennes framework, we analyze the phase-dependent ABS spectrum and investigate how time-dependent superconducting phase ramps drive nonadiabatic Landau-Zener transitions across the avoided level crossing. The resulting excited-state population is characterized using the ergotropy formalism to quantify the maximum extractable work. Analytical expressions relating junction transparency, phase-ramp duration, excitation probability, and ergotropy are obtained, providing insight into the charging dynamics. We further discuss the scaling of the maximum extractable work with the spin and valley degeneracies of graphene and the number of transverse ballistic modes, and estimate representative charging times and output power using experimentally reported graphene-Al junction parameters. Our results provide a quantum thermodynamic interpretation of phase-controlled ABS dynamics and illustrate the potential of graphene SNS Josephson junctions as a platform for coherent energy storage studies.
articles.summary_en: Researchers model graphene superconductor–normal–superconductor junctions as platforms for coherent quantum energy storage. The study quantifies extractable work, charging dynamics and output-power estimates using graphene–aluminum junction parameters, but reports no commercial demonstration.

articles.title_original: Preparation and Stability Study of Graphene/R141b Nanofluids for Heat Transfer Enhancement
articles.title_en: Study Stabilizes Graphene/R141b Nanofluids for Heat Transfer
articles.excerpt_original: The instability of nanofluids leads to particle agglomeration and sedimentation, which clog the heat transfer channels and deteriorate the overall performance of heat exchangers. Accordingly, preparing uniformly dispersed and structurally stable nanofluids serves as a fundamental prerequisite for their practical engineering applications. In this study, refrigerant R141b was selected as the base fluid, and graphene/R141b nanofluids were prepared via a two-step method assisted by ultrasonic oscillation. The effects of ultrasonic oscillation time, dosage of surfactant, and nanoparticle mass concentration on the stability of graphene/R141b were systematically investigated, and zeta potential, DLS particle size, Raman and XRD analysis were used to evaluate the stability of graphene/R141b. The experimental results demonstrate that ultrasonic oscillation time and nanoparticle mass concentration both exert significant influences on the stability of graphene/R141b nanofluid. The SDS surfactant can effectively improve the stability of the prepared graphene/R141b nanofluid. In conclusion, under the conditions of adding SDS surfactant and carrying out ultrasonic oscillation within 120–150 min, graphene/R141b with a mass concentration ranging from 0.05% to 0.4% exhibits satisfactory stability, while excessively prolonged sonication (180 min) reduces the stability of the nanofluid, which provides a promising candidate for future validation of heat-transfer-enhancement performance in heat-exchanger applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers investigated how ultrasonic treatment, surfactant dosage and graphene concentration affect the stability of graphene/R141b nanofluids. SDS and 120–150 minutes of sonication produced satisfactory stability at 0.05–0.4% graphene concentration, supporting further evaluation for heat-exchanger applications.

articles.title_original: Valley Hall viscosity in gapped graphene with and without a magnetic field
articles.title_en: Study Clarifies Valley Hall Viscosity in Gapped Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Hall viscosity is conventionally defined through the stress response to time-dependent strain, a perturbation that is difficult to implement in solid-state experiments. We formulate a related viscoelastic response to static, spatially inhomogeneous electric fields and compare it with the strain-based response. For gapped graphene in a perpendicular magnetic field, the two formulations give the same Landau-level response, whose Hall viscosity is asymmetric between the two valleys. At zero magnetic field, a valley-even quantum-metric coefficient combines with the valley-odd Hall conductivity to produce equal and opposite valley-resolved responses; global time-reversal symmetry therefore forces the net Hall viscosity to vanish. In an insulating state, exact particle--hole symmetry eliminates this zero-field response, whereas particle--hole-symmetry breaking generates a cutoff-dependent geometric contribution from the occupied Fermi sea. These results connect valley-dependent viscoelasticity with electromagnetic response in gapped Dirac materials and clarify the conditions under which a valley Hall viscosity can arise.
articles.summary_en: Researchers develop a static electric-field formulation of Hall viscosity and compare it with the conventional strain-based response. The study finds valley-dependent effects in magnetic fields, while time-reversal and particle–hole symmetries suppress or modify the response at zero field.

articles.title_original: Multilayer PDMS/PMMA@MXene composite films for dual-functional electromagnetic shielding and photothermal conversion
articles.title_en: Multilayer MXene Films Combine EMI Shielding with Photothermal Conversion
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Flexible multifunctional polymer-based films for electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding are of great value in 5G communication technology, wearable electronics, and related fields. Here, a series of PDMS/PMMA@MXene multilayer composite films was constructed on the basis of an alternating P–M–P design, with PMMA microspheres serving as spacers; the preparation combined vacuum-assisted filtration with spray coating and curing. In such a porous, multilayer architecture, the film containing seven MXene layers (M7) delivered an EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SE) of up to 57.4 dB at 10 GHz in the X-band (8.2–12.4 GHz), and the shielding was dominated by absorption loss. The films also converted light into heat efficiently: under an irradiance of 1000 W/m², the saturation temperature reached 61°C, and the photothermal response stayed stable over repeated cycles. These flexible multilayer films, which combine effective EMI shielding with photothermal conversion, are promising candidates for electromagnetic protection of electronic devices and for solar thermal utilization.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed flexible PDMS/PMMA@MXene multilayer films achieving up to 57.4 dB EMI shielding at 10 GHz, primarily through absorption. The films also reached 61°C under 1000 W/m² irradiation with stable repeated photothermal cycling, supporting potential use in electronic protection and solar-thermal applications.

articles.title_original: Metal-organic framework/MXene composites: design strategies and applications for energy storage, catalysis, and sensing
articles.title_en: MOF/MXene Composites Advance Energy Storage, Catalysis and Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), as crystalline porous materials with tunable chemical compositions, have attracted widespread interest for energy-related applications. However, their low electrical conductivity and limited structural stability under electrochemical conditions restrict practical deployment. Integrating MOFs with two-dimensional transition metal carbides/nitrides (MXenes) creates composite materials that combine the high surface area and active sites of MOFs with the metallic conductivity and mechanical flexibility of MXenes. This review summarizes recent progress on MOF/MXene composites. The major synthetic routes are classified into four categories: in situ growth with interfacial chemical bonding, electrostatic self-assembly, post-synthetic transformation into metal oxides, sulfides, and phosphides, and interface engineering. Their applications are discussed across electrochemical energy storage (lithium, sodium, potassium, and zinc-ion batteries, and supercapacitors), energy conversion (electrocatalytic hydrogen/oxygen evolution, oxygen reduction, and photocatalysis), and sensing. Despite research advances, challenges remain for practical application, including MXene oxidation during processing and operation, difficulties in large-scale fabrication with batch-to-batch consistency, and the need for precise interfacial regulation. Finally, future research directions are outlined, including artificial intelligence-assisted material screening, construction of three-dimensional hierarchical structures, and evaluation of industrial applicability through standardized testing protocols.
articles.summary_en: A review categorizes four design strategies for metal-organic framework/MXene composites and surveys their use in batteries, supercapacitors, electrocatalysis and sensors. Key barriers include MXene oxidation, inconsistent large-scale fabrication and limited interfacial control.

articles.title_original: Vanadium Oxide/MXene Composite Fiber Cathodes With Superior Spinnability Enabling High Electrochemical Performance for Fiber‐Shaped Zinc‐Ion Batteries
articles.title_en: MXene–Vanadium Oxide Fiber Cathodes Improve Zinc-Ion Battery Performance
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Fiber‐shaped zinc‐ion batteries are highly deformable and can store energy in irregular spaces. Fiber cathodes with carbon fiber cores can be continuously prepared via wet spinning. In this work, MXene is introduced into the cathode by directly hybridizing with vanadium oxide, acting as a bridge to enhance the interfacial interaction within the cathode. MXene modifies the rheological behavior of the cathode slurry and facilitates the rearrangement of the active material during wet spinning, thereby effectively improving fiber spinnability and mitigating agglomeration of the active material. Additionally, MXene enhances the electrical conductivity of the active material and stabilizes the structure of VO 2 , enabling the composite cathode to deliver satisfactory specific capacity and cycling stability. The cathode achieves a specific capacity of 136 mAh g −1 at 3 A g −1 after 2000 cycles, which is 109% higher than that of the pure VO 2 cathode. The cathodes are assembled with MXene/chitosan‐coated fiber anodes and a hydrogel electrolyte to make full batteries. The resulting battery packs can power lighting and communication modules in small unmanned aerial vehicles. This work leverages the multiple advantages of MXene in various dimensions, proposes an optimization strategy for carbon‐fiber‐based fiber‐shaped batteries, and highlights their application potential.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed wet-spun vanadium oxide/MXene composite fiber cathodes that improve spinnability, conductivity, and structural stability in fiber-shaped zinc-ion batteries. The cathodes retained 136 mAh g−1 at 3 A g−1 after 2,000 cycles, and assembled batteries powered lighting and communication modules in small unmanned aerial vehicles.

articles.title_original: 3D printing of boron nitride polymer composites for tailored thermal transport and mechanical performance
articles.title_en: 3D-printed boron nitride composites enable tailored thermal transport
articles.excerpt_original: Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) microplatelets are layered structural materials known for their thermal stability, chemical resistance, electrical insulation, and anisotropic thermal transport behaviors. They are highly thermally conductive in-plane yet possess relatively low through-plane conductivity and as a result their orientation plays a critical role in the overall thermal transport performance of h-BN/polymer composites. In this study, masked stereolithography (MSLA) 3D printing approach was used to investigate how h-BN platelet size, filler loading, and printing layer thickness affect platelet alignment, heat transfer, and mechanical behavior. Three types of h-BN microplatelets with average lateral sizes of 0.9, 12, and 45 μm were incorporated into a UV curable resin at loadings up to 20 wt% and printed with layer thicknesses of 10–50 μm. The characterization results from X-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy showed that larger h-BN platelets aligned more effectively along the printing plane, especially when thinner layers were used. This alignment improved in-plane thermal transport, with the highest thermal conductivity obtained for the BN45 composite printed at a 10 μm layer thickness. Mechanical testing showed that BN addition generally increased the elastic modulus, while tensile strength showed a more composition-dependent trend. Overall, these results show that MSLA 3D printing can tune h-BN platelet orientation through filler size and layer thickness, providing a practical route to effectively tailor the thermal and mechanical behavior of BN/polymer composites.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used masked stereolithography to control boron nitride platelet alignment in polymer composites by varying platelet size, filler loading, and print-layer thickness. Larger platelets and thinner layers improved in-plane thermal conductivity, while boron nitride generally increased elastic modulus.

articles.title_original: Evidence for a charged vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid
articles.title_en: Evidence of a Charged Vortex Lattice in Graphene Bilayer Exciton Superfluid
articles.excerpt_original: Lattices of quantized vortices are a defining property of rotating superfluids and of type-II superconductors in magnetic fields. Realizing an analogous vortex lattice in an exciton superfluid-formed from bound electron-hole pairs-has remained challenging because excitons are electrically neutral. Building on previous theoretical studies of the low-energy excitations in an exciton superfluid, recent theory has predicted that in a strong magnetic field, a weakly charged exciton superfluid can stabilize a vortex-antivortex lattice arising from the mutual repulsion of fractionally charged vortex cores. Here we report evidence for this predicted vortex lattice in a bilayer exciton condensate by imaging its charged vortices with the scanning tunnelling microscope. The condensate forms between Landau levels of two graphene layers separated by a thin hexagonal boron nitride barrier in a perpendicular magnetic field. We find that the vortex lattice periodicity scales with the total excess charge and is insensitive to its distribution between the two layers, in quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions. Our observations provide evidence for phase coherence in an exciton superfluid system.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report imaging a predicted vortex–antivortex lattice in an exciton condensate formed between two graphene layers separated by hexagonal boron nitride. The findings provide experimental evidence of phase coherence in a charged exciton superfluid and support theoretical predictions linking lattice periodicity to total excess charge.
