articles.summary_en: Researchers fabricated a pn-junction photodetector using partially fluorinated p-type graphene and sputtered n-type indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A 200 μm patterned ITO structure reduced dark current by 120-fold compared with an unpatterned 5:5 electrode configuration under 468 nm illumination.

articles.title_original: Ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene: Dynamical skyrmion lattices and their excitations
articles.title_en: Rhombohedral graphene hosts dynamical skyrmion lattices
articles.excerpt_original: We introduce an interacting ideal limit of rhombohedral graphene in which interactions spontaneously generate a correlated Chern insulator. Our analysis reveals that this Chern insulator can be understood as a layer-pseudospin skyrmion lattice stabilized by electronic interactions, and that it gives rise to genuine skyrmion lattice physics, complete with dynamics. This dynamical skyrmion lattice naturally leads to experimentally measurable consequences. In particular, we identify new collective excitations corresponding to chiral shape deformations of the skyrmions, and propose a new positively charged quasiparticle, the skyrmion vacancy. These results establish a qualitatively new form of moiré Chern physics in rhombohedral graphene: an interaction-generated skyrmion lattice whose skyrmions are dynamical low-energy degrees of freedom.
articles.summary_en: Researchers propose an interaction-generated skyrmion lattice in rhombohedral graphene linked to a correlated Chern insulator. The theoretical framework predicts chiral collective excitations and a positively charged skyrmion-vacancy quasiparticle, offering experimentally testable signatures of moiré Chern physics.

articles.title_original: Room-temperature multiferroic semiconductor with electrically switchable valley polarization in Zn-/Cd-intercalated $\mathrm{CrSe_2}$
articles.title_en: Zn- and Cd-intercalated CrSe₂ predicted as room-temperature ferrovalley semiconductors
articles.excerpt_original: Purely electrical switching of ferromagnetism-induced valley polarization in two dimensional (2D) ferrovalley materials provides a promising avenue for low-power information processing. Herein, Zn- and Cd-intercalated CrSe _{2} 2 (denoted XCrSe _{2} 2 , X = Zn, Cd) are predicted by first-principles calculations to be room-temperature ferrovalley semiconductors, in which valley polarization can be switched by reversing the ferroelectric (FE) polarization. The intercalated atoms break inversion symmetry and generate in-plane and out-of-plane FE polarizations with low switching barriers and polar distortions stable above room temperature in AIMD simulations. The superexchange of t_{2g} t 2 g and e_g e g of Cr atoms dominates the ferromagnetic (FM) coupling with Curie temperature near 350 K and out-of-plane easy axis. The ferromagnetism together with spin-orbit coupling lifts the K/K ' ′ valley degeneracy and produces spin-polarized valley splitting. Crucially, FE reversal strongly modifies the electronic structure and valley-resolved states, enabling electrical control of the valley splitting, and ferroelectrically switchable anomalous valley Hall effect in a single material platform. Our results establish monolayer XCrSe _2 2 as a rare 2D multiferroic semiconductor combining robust FE and FM orders with nonvolatile electrical control of valley degrees of freedom.
articles.summary_en: First-principles calculations predict Zn- and Cd-intercalated monolayer CrSe₂ could combine ferromagnetism and ferroelectricity above room temperature. Reversing ferroelectric polarization is predicted to electrically switch valley polarization and the anomalous valley Hall effect, indicating potential for low-power valleytronic devices.

articles.title_original: Synergistic Interfacial Engineering in V2C MXene Heterostructures for Enhanced Nano-aluminum Reactivity
articles.title_en: V2C MXene Heterostructures Boost Nano-Aluminum Reactivity
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Nano-aluminum (nano-Al) is a high-energy-density material with exceptional reactivity, making it promising for aerospace and military applications. Reducing particle size increases the active surface area and interfacial mass diffusion, but intrinsic agglomeration and dense alumina shells hinder diffusion. Conventional additives often reduce reactivity. Here, we modulate nano-Al interfacial diffusion through synergistic interactions in a V2C MXene heterostructure. The self-assembly of nano-Al on MXene suppresses agglomeration, while fluorine-containing terminations etch the alumina shells. The heterostructure also forms metal oxide contact layers that promote solid-phase thermite reactions. These effects increase the peak heat flow in air to 107.6 W g−1, 3.5 times that of pristine nano-Al. Solid-phase reactions complete energy release before Al melting, minimizing energy loss. The composite shows larger flame areas and a lower minimum ignition concentration (≥5 wt %). Adjusting the heating temperature reduces the total combustion duration by 88.9% and increases the dynamic pressure. This versatile fabrication process enables tunable performance for diverse operational environments.
articles.summary_en: ACS-published research reports that V2C MXene heterostructures suppress nano-aluminum agglomeration and etch alumina shells, increasing peak heat flow to 107.6 W g−1. The composite also shortened combustion duration and increased dynamic pressure, indicating potential for aerospace and military energetic-material applications.

articles.title_original: Quantum batteries in two-dimensional material-based Josephson junctions
articles.title_en: Graphene-Based Josephson Junction Proposed for Quantum Batteries
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract We investigate the solid-state implementation of a Dicke-like quantum battery consisting of a two-dimensional material-based Josephson junction inductively coupled to a resonator, using graphene as a representative example. In this configuration, Andreev bound states naturally act as non-interacting, energetically non-degenerate two-level systems, and the setup allows for both single-photon and two-photon resonant processes. The coupling between the LC-circuit flux and the supercurrent through the junction gives rise to peculiar longitudinal interaction terms that have no counterpart in the conventional Dicke model. We demonstrate that these additional couplings can enhance energy storage for a proper range of parameters. The proposed architecture also enables an alternative, but comparable, charging protocol that relies on tuning the superconducting phase difference across the junction.
articles.summary_en: Researchers propose a solid-state quantum battery using a graphene-based Josephson junction coupled to a resonator. The design exploits Andreev bound states and tunable superconducting-phase differences to enhance energy storage under suitable conditions.

academic.blurb: Characterization of the same PECVD-grown graphene samples links lower-temperature, large-area copper-foil growth with measured optical and thermal properties. Monolayers grown at 600–800°C showed 97.7% visible transmission, while thermal conductivity declined from about 3,000 W/m-K at 300 K to 800 W/m-K at 1,000 K.

Attosecond-precision subcycle band-structure videography visualized strong-field electron motion and non-adiabatic tunnelling across graphene’s first Brillouin zone. The work supplies direct experimental insight into coherent electronic control and scattering, rather than only inferring these processes from aggregate electronic measurements.

This systematic review finds graphene oxide, reduced graphene oxide and graphene quantum dots effective against pharmaceuticals, heavy metals and other wastewater contaminants through adsorption, catalysis and membrane filtration. Its value is tempered by aggregation, fouling, regeneration losses, toxicity, cost, scalability and inconsistent standards that remain deployment barriers.
